title: COMOG press conference calls for Ghanaian state action on LGBTQI policy
scope: One local press conference; a separate threatened future demonstration is not treated as executed.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Graphic Online confirms a press conference but supplies no attendee count; no threshold inference is made from the event type or organizer.

title.summary: Graphic Online reports COMOG held a press conference opposing LGBTQI activities and calling for action by Ghanaian institutions.

start_date.summary: The Feb. 25 report describes the press conference as occurring "yesterday," identifying Feb. 24, 2021.

location.summary: Graphic Online locates the press conference in Accra.

organizer.summary: The report identifies the Coalition of Muslim Organisations Ghana (COMOG) as the organizer.

demands.summary: The report says COMOG called on the Ghanaian government to support a counselling/treatment centre and on Parliament to condemn diplomatic missions. social_restrictions is a provisional fit to the reported LGBTQI policy issue; retain the original wording in notes.

participants.summary: The reviewed article scope gives no attendance number; no count is inferred.

end_date.summary: No physical end time or duration is given.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; no event-specific account of participant violence is established.

state_response.summary: No government response to the press conference is described in the reviewed scope; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: The gathering and a domestic institutional call are reported, but the >=50 public-meeting threshold is not established.

notes: Research lead, not an approved record. S022 is a limited contemporaneous body read. The domestic-state calls are distinguishable from the separate demand directed at foreign missions. S020 has a GNA byline and a cache-miss retrieval failure; S021 is a search-only COMOG statement. They are not counted as independent confirmations. The category social_restrictions is provisional. Do not infer that the announced "mammoth demonstration" happened.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend the Feb. 24 public press conference?
Was the meeting open to the public in the sense used by the historical manual?
Can the exact domestic demand be mapped to social_restrictions under the additional Coding Procedure?
Did the conditional future demonstration occur, and if so when and where?
Did Ghanaian state authorities accommodate, ignore, disperse, arrest, beat, kill, or shoot in response?

title: Ada Songor Feb. 5 protest/confrontation lead at Electrochem operations
location: Salom-Madagber / Toflokpo-Salom, Ada West District; exact locality naming varies across reports
scope: Possible separate local action at the start of Electrochem operations; its classification as a public protest is not established.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. No attendance figure is reported in the reviewed material. Reported injuries, arrests or armed persons are not turnout.

title.summary: S023 search results call the Feb. 5 event a protest; the limited S024 body read describes a reported invasion at Salom-Madagber. S025–S027 offer conflicting or retrospective discovery leads. Whether this was a qualifying public protest remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: The search-only MFWA result dates the claimed protest to Feb. 5 when operations commenced. S024 body separately recounts a Feb. 5 invasion allegation; the other records are search-only.

location.summary: Retrospective reporting uses Salom-Madagber and Toflokpo-Salom for the community/location; exact local naming is not reconciled.

demands.summary: A search result quotes a later statement that community members raised issues over the Songor lease, but no body was opened and no precise demand directed to the Ghanaian state is established; no demand category is assigned.

participants.summary: No total crowd or >=50 attendance figure is stated. Injuries and arrests are not turnout.

end_date.summary: No physical end or continuity boundary is established.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown. Allegations describe armed attacks or clashes but do not establish event-specific violence by protesters against the state.

state_response.summary: Attribution is disputed in search-only material and the limited retrospective body scope reports allegations rather than an event-specific verified state response; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: Only search results identify a protest; the opened retrospective describes a petition allegation of an invasion. Occurrence as a public gathering, >=50 threshold, and a demand to Ghanaian state policy are not established.

notes: Search-only evidence remains the sole source explicitly calling the Feb. 5 gathering a protest (S023). S024 is an opened retrospective with limited scope, summarizing claims in a 2023 petition; it separately dates the Jan. 27 shootings and does not itself establish a Feb. 5 public protest. S025 search results report police denial of involvement while describing hired thugs; do not infer official shootings. S026 and S024 are from the same MFWA project. This may relate thematically to January candidate GHA202101-E002, but no continuous gathering or event merge is established.
open_questions: Was there a public protest or only a violent confrontation at the site?
What demand, if any, did participants direct to Ghanaian government policy rather than the private company?
Did at least 50 people gather at one time?
Who organized the action, and what was the exact location?
Who shot or injured community members, and were police acting in an official capacity?
When did the physical gathering begin and end?
Is this a distinct Feb. 5 event, a phase of the Jan. 27 action, or a different incident within the same dispute?
